page: Google Cloud Platform x5-2064-48t-metal is a bare-metal server configuration engineered for extreme memory-intensive workloads. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the platform features 2,064 dedicated vCPUs and 49,152 GB of system memory, achieving an allocation of 23.81 GB of RAM per vCPU. The hardware contains no graphical processing units (0 GPUs) and does not bundle local disk storage.

Because local storage is absent, the system requires network-attached storage for operating system images and persistent data persistence. Compute resources are completely dedicated rather than shared or virtualized. Network provisioning provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating internal private VPC routing or network address translation for outside network connectivity.

The 48 TB memory capacity paired with 2,064 dedicated cores creates a resource profile tailored for scale-up computing. The platform fits large-scale enterprise resource planning systems, in-memory databases such as SAP HANA, massive real-time data analytics, and extensive graph databases that require single-node memory residency without distributed partitioning.
description: Google Cloud Platform x5-2064-48t-metal is a bare-metal, memory-optimized server configuration based on the x86_64 CPU architecture. Designed for massive scale memory requirements, the server provides 2,064 dedicated physical vCPUs paired with 49,152 GB of system memory, establishing a high memory density of 23.81 GB per vCPU. Hardware accelerators are absent, with a GPU count of zero, and the platform provides no onboard local disk storage, requiring external network-attached storage solutions for all persistent disk input and output operations. Network configuration does not bundle complimentary public IPv4 addresses, relying entirely on virtual private cloud networking architectures. This extreme ratio of memory capacity to dedicated processing units positions the server for single-node in-memory computing tasks. Appropriate operational workloads include ultra-large enterprise resource planning databases, massive in-memory analytics engines, continuous real-time data processing, and enterprise memory-bound data structures requiring tens of terabytes of uninterrupted addressable space.
